features/feature_dot.description: Compare fixed points, labeled points and a continuously moving tracer.
walkthrough: Axes maps curve coordinates through c2p. Ordinary dots identify selected points; AnnotationDot and LabeledDot attach different kinds of explanation to a location.
The glowing tracer advances its parameter using elapsed time, while other dots stay at their chosen coordinates. Its motion comes from an updater, not from the initial reveal animation.
experiments: Freeze the tracer’s parameter and change its glow radius. Compare an appearance change with movement along the curve.

features/feature_equation.description: Match vector-text characters across an anagram and an algebra step.
walkthrough: The first transformation changes LISTEN to SILENT after decomposing the Text entities into characters. TransformMatchingText can associate matching glyphs even when their order changes.
The second transformation changes 3x = 9 to x = 3 and colors selected characters. This example uses vector Text rather than a LaTeX typesetter; the strings themselves supply the algebra.
experiments: Replace the anagram with another pair containing repeated letters. Inspect how matching and unmatched characters move.

features/feature_number_plane.description: Plot two waves and label selected points on a coordinate grid.
walkthrough: NumberPlane combines axes and grid lines. Its plotting helpers convert mathematical coordinates into scene geometry, so changing physical width differs from changing xRange.
The sine wave and damped wave share that coordinate mapping. Their reveal animations introduce already-defined curves and labels in a controlled order.
experiments: Double the plane width without changing its coordinate ranges. Compare the waves’ displayed spacing with their mathematical period.

features/feature_plot_function.description: Compare an explicit curve with a sampled radial surface.
walkthrough: The upper Axes plots a function of x; the lower ThreeDAxes hosts a SurfaceGraph3D. An orbit controller lets you inspect the spatial surface from another angle.

The surface callback handles radius zero explicitly. The curve’s fractional powers also need a valid input domain: negative bases can produce NaN for noninteger exponents. Keep domain validity separate from the staged view-style changes.
experiments: Restrict the explicit curve to positive x, then change its exponent. Compare that geometry change with changing only the surface shading style.

features/feature_plot_implicit.description: Draw a two-dimensional relation and a three-dimensional torus without solving for a dependent coordinate.
walkthrough: ImplicitCurve2DGPU receives a WGSL expression in x and y. Its zero set defines the visible curve, so the function need not be expressible as y = f(x).
ImplicitSurface3D evaluates a torus relation in three variables. The axes and staged view styles help you inspect the same zero set as a spatial surface.
experiments: Change the torus major radius while holding the minor radius fixed. Compare the hole size with the thickness of the tube.

features/feature_plot_parametric.description: Sample a helix and a torus from parameter callbacks.
walkthrough: ParametricCurve3D converts a single parameter into a Vec3. ParametricSurface3D converts two parameters into a Vec3; their ranges and segment counts control which geometry gets sampled.
The custom shader changes color and alpha on the surface. It changes the visible treatment of the existing geometry, while changing the callback changes the mesh itself.
experiments: Increase the helix parameter range without changing its step. Then increase the torus segment count and compare extent with sampling density.

features/feature_polar_axes.description: Draw a rose curve and a spiral in polar coordinates.
walkthrough: PolarAxes.plotPolar interprets the callback result as radius at an angle measured in radians. The rose oscillates in radius; the spiral increases radius with angle.
Each curve is created in sequence so its shape can be followed. A negative rose radius is meaningful in polar coordinates and does not represent an invalid Cartesian point.
experiments: Change cos(4 * theta) to cos(3 * theta), then compare the petals over the same angular interval.

features/feature_primitive_shader_showca.description: Combine mathematical geometry with gradient effects on its stroke and fill.
walkthrough: The scene plots a wave and adds area and Riemann-rectangle representations. PathEffectGradient styles the contour; FillEffectLinearGradient styles filled regions.
A ValueTracker drives the wave’s function updates. That changes geometry, while the gradient effects change how the resulting geometry is shaded.
experiments: Keep the tracker fixed and alter one gradient stop. Then restore the tracker animation to separate paint changes from changing curve shape.

features/feature_surface.description: Inspect a checkerboard Gaussian surface with an orbit camera.
walkthrough: ParametricSurface3D samples a Gaussian bump over u and v. Its checkerboard colors make the grid of surface patches visible, and ThreeDAxes supplies a spatial reference.
The active example remains a static Gaussian after its waits. The proposed ripple and rotation updates are commented out, so they do not animate the visible surface.
experiments: Enable just surface.updateFunction in the commented updater. Compare the resulting height changes with the original static bump before enabling rotation.

features/feature_threed_axes.description: Place a helix and a radial ripple on the same spatial axes.
walkthrough: ThreeDAxes supplies the coordinate frame. A parametric callback creates the helix, while a height callback creates the ripple surface and handles its center without division by zero.
The axes and helix are drawn before the surface fades in. Orbiting the camera helps reveal how the curve sits relative to the surface rather than changing either mathematical definition.
experiments: Change the helix’s vertical coefficient from 0.3 to 0.6. Compare its pitch with the unchanged ripple surface.

features/feature_vector_field_3d.description: Inspect a sampled vector field with two poles and a rotational component.
walkthrough: The callback combines attraction toward two poles with a curl-like term. VectorField3D displays sampled arrows; this scene does not integrate particle trajectories.
The grouped axes and field rotate together while updateField refreshes the arrow data. Sampling and camera motion remain separate from the vector formula.
experiments: Set the rotational term’s coefficient to zero. Compare arrow directions near the poles with the original swirling field.

features/feature_vector_field_fluid.description: Follow streamlines through an analytic, pointer-influenced vector field.
walkthrough: VectorField2D and Streamlines2D share the same time-dependent callback. One shows local directions; the other makes longer motion through those directions easier to follow.
The pointer is unprojected through the camera and converted with axes.p2c. The formula is a prescribed field, rather than a Navier–Stokes solver evolving pressure and incompressibility.
experiments: Freeze the time value in the callback and move the pointer. Then freeze the pointer position to isolate the time-dependent flow.

features/inspector_test_scene.description: Explore an entity fixture containing styled paths, typography and pointer handling.
walkthrough: The scene creates several entities with different geometry and paint settings. The builder-generated hexagon has a click handler, providing an event target as well as a visible shape.
This source serves as an inspector fixture. The documentation preview runs the scene; the separate Studio inspector is not embedded in that preview.
experiments: Change the hexagon’s join or cap settings, click it, and inspect the browser console message from its handler.

features/math_shape.description: Compare wireframe and fill on a box, sphere and torus.
walkthrough: MathShape factories create spatial primitives with their own mesh topology. Positions separate them, while fill and stroke settings expose faces and edges together.
The updater rotates each shape using elapsed time. The orbit controller changes your view independently, making it possible to inspect the rotating geometry from a fixed or moving camera.
experiments: Disable one shape’s fill while keeping its stroke. Compare the resulting wireframe with the filled neighboring primitives.

features/model_manim_shading_showcase.description: Compare solid and checkerboard treatments across spatial primitives.
walkthrough: Box, Sphere, Cylinder and Torus supply different surfaces. Their shading options control color treatment; checkerboard colors reveal patches without changing the underlying mesh topology.
SDFText titles are marked as UI, while the models rotate in world space. This keeps the labels readable as the camera and models move.
experiments: Enable checkerboard shading on a solid sphere. Compare the apparent surface structure with the same sphere’s unchanged silhouette.

features/noise_1d.description: Compare seven families and combinations of one-dimensional noise.
walkthrough: The stacked curves sample white, Perlin, simplex, value and Worley noise, followed by fractal and ridged variants. Vertical offsets keep the curves readable.
Seed, sampling scale and time offset all affect the comparison. Hold those choices steady when investigating a generator instead of attributing every difference to its name.
experiments: Freeze time and use the same input scale for Perlin and simplex. Then change only their seed and compare continuity.

features/noise_curl_2d.description: Turn scalar noise into a flowing two-dimensional vector field.
walkthrough: The field combines macro and micro noise before sampleCurl2D produces directions. VectorField2D shows those directions as arrows rather than rendering the scalar noise as brightness.
The updater also changes axis ranges, affecting which part of the field is sampled. Fix the ranges when comparing the contribution of the two noise scales.
experiments: Remove the micro-noise contribution and keep the axes fixed. Compare broad circulation with the original smaller variations.

features/noise_scalers.description: Reshape noise into quantized, remapped terrain heights.
walkthrough: NoiseScaler wraps a Perlin source and applies quantization, output-range mapping and a power curve. SurfaceGraph3D samples the transformed values as heights.
The input offsets move through the noise field over time. Color stops expose height bands, so a stepped surface can be read independently of its motion.
experiments: Reduce the number of quantization steps. Compare terrace spacing while leaving the output range and power curve unchanged.

features/noise.description: Build a moving terrain from several noise scales.
walkthrough: A domain-warped Perlin component supplies broad terrain. Worley detail and smaller simplex samples add structure at other scales before the height values are combined.
The surface updater changes sample coordinates with time. This moves through a fixed procedural definition rather than loading successive mesh assets.
experiments: Remove the smallest ripple contribution. Compare the terrain silhouette and local texture with the full combination.

features/polyhedra_prisms_showcase.description: Compare Platonic solids with prisms of different bases.
walkthrough: MathShape factories produce a box, tetrahedron, octahedron and several prisms. Their positions and labels let you compare faces and edges without changing the camera.
Rotation and bobbing come from elapsed-time updates. The prism’s base definition determines topology; animation only changes its transform.
experiments: Replace the triangular prism base with four sides. Inspect the new faces before changing its rotation speed.

features/timescale.description: Slow the scene clock while several animations overlap.
walkthrough: Some play calls are intentionally not awaited, allowing text, movement and morphing to overlap. TracePath makes the model’s motion easier to compare across the timing changes.

animateTimeScale eases the scene clock toward a small positive rate and later back to one. Scene waits also follow that clock, so a short timeline wait can take much longer in wall time during slow motion.
experiments: Change the slow-motion target from 0.02 to 0.2. Compare elapsed wall time while leaving animation durations unchanged.

features/track_animation_demo.description: Give a composite telemetry card its own staged creation animation.
walkthrough: TelemetryCard extends Entity and attaches its frame, labels, beacon and sparkline as children. Its createAnim hook receives a TrackBuilder that describes how those pieces enter.

Each t.add call starts a stage; animations passed in that call run together. t.wait separates stages. Create invokes the composite hook, letting callers introduce the card without repeating its internal sequence.
experiments: Move the sparkline Create into its own t.add stage. Compare the changed order with increasing its duration inside the existing parallel stage.
